initial.claims: For finite abelian G acting on simple purely infinite Cuntz–Krieger algebra with finite essential 0–1 matrix by workshop diagonal quasi-free automorphisms (span preserved, every canonical range projection fixed), fixed-algebra unitaries approximately implement each element independently. The edge-diagonal graph theorem is for finite strongly connected graph with edges and excluding a directed-cycle graph.
initial.initial: All graph phase automorphisms lie in a product torus and commute with equivariant homotopies. For an inner phase automorphism, the fixed diagonal MASA forces implementer there. Closed periodic units imply phase product one, yielding a normalized vertex coboundary. Choose paths once for every group element to extend phases to a genuine fixed vertex representation. Removing it factors the action through pointwise outer G/K; uniqueness for each g gives approximate conjugacy with uniform finite-group invariance, corrected by averaging and polar decomposition. Reintroduce exact honest cocycle and average in original fixed algebra. Graph identification with edge operators s_i p_j verified by orthogonal terminal projections.
initial.questions: Verify Gabe–Szabó exact equivariance, unital hypotheses, shift absorption and target assumptions. Graph theorem scope syntax must be read as excluding the graph consisting of a directed cycle; the proof and the main matrix theorem explicitly exclude that case. Check periodic, nonouter, nonfaithful, trivial quotient and graph range conventions; no representation law on approximate implementing unitaries.

math: Finite abelian actions preserving generator span and fixing each range projection necessarily scale each generator by a character. A finite essential 0–1 matrix gives the equivalent edge graph via s_i p_j. The simple purely infinite hypothesis forces a strongly connected graph which is not a directed cycle. For the finite strongly connected noncycle graph the standard path diagonal is a MASA. A phase action implemented by a diagonal unitary has trivial cycle phase by periodic infinite paths and therefore lies in the vertex coboundaries. Choose base paths once to construct a genuine vertex-phase representation across the whole group. Its removal changes the action to an outer quotient even in the nonsplit case; target unitaries from unital equivariant uniqueness are approximately fixed under the full finite quotient and can be averaged and polar-corrected. The honest vertex cocycle lifts implementing limits back into the original fixed algebra. The trivial quotient, nonfaithful actions and periodic graphs are covered.
ambiguity: Page 3 says 'with at least one edge which is not a directed cycle'. The proof and page 4 use a finite strongly connected graph with edges which is not itself a directed cycle. The main matrix theorem explicitly excludes a cycle. If the modifier is attached to edge, the auxiliary formulation would admit a directed two-cycle and be false: choose order-two phases (-1,1) to negate the central circle coordinate in M_2(C(T)); a norm limit of inner automorphisms fixes the center. Treat the antecedent as the graph, consistently with the actual proof, section 4 and the earlier same-proof source wording. Record this editorial ambiguity explicitly; original manuscript untouched.
